title: Anthropogenic host redistribution expands butterfly resource geography across the specialization spectrum

central_claim.text: Anthropogenic redistribution of larval host plants expands butterfly resource geography broadly across specialization classes, but similar proportional gains are assembled through concentrated host contributions in family specialists and distributed portfolios in generalists; this decoupling reveals taxonomic, portfolio, geographic and climatic specialization as partially coupled but non-interchangeable ecological dimensions.

claims.claim: Family-level host breadth only partially tracks geographic larval-resource breadth.
claims.evidence: 239-species exact S1 resource reconstruction; host-taxonomy adequate sensitivity subset n=215.

claims.claim: Introduced host ranges expand reconstructed geographic resource opportunity for most butterflies without a proportional expansion advantage for broad family-level generalists.
claims.key_statistic: 86.2% expanded; Spearman host-family breadth vs log proportional expansion rho=0.008

claims.claim: Similar aggregate anthropogenic expansion is assembled through more concentrated host contributions in specialists and more distributed host portfolios in generalists.
claims.key_statistic: rho host-family breadth vs effective contributor number=0.492; rho vs maximum single-host share=-0.486

claims.claim: Species-level host richness reveals hierarchical specialization within fixed family-level breadth categories.
claims.evidence: 82 expanded one-family species plus within-stratum analyses.
claims.key_statistic: one-family rho resolved host species vs effective contributors=0.734; vs maximum single-host share=-0.707

claims.claim: Climate commonly filters realized butterfly geography within reconstructed contemporary larval-resource opportunity.
claims.evidence: 24 independent climate-informative species after frozen quality gates and uniform transport completion.
claims.key_statistic: median filtering score=0.801; 23/24 >0.5; 22/24 positive mismatch delta

claims.claim: Broader host-family diets do not detectably weaken climate filtering after contemporary resource breadth is controlled.
claims.key_statistic: partial Spearman rho=-0.166; one-sided Freedman-Lane p=0.2237; n=24

forbidden_overclaims: Introduced host distributions caused butterfly range expansion.
Every reconstructed introduced-host region is currently used by the butterfly.
Host-family breadth has no ecological importance.
Climate alone determines realized butterfly distributions.
Species-level host portfolio structure explains climate filtering in the current independent data.
The post-gate transport completion was fully response-blind.
Exploratory resource analyses are confirmatory tests.

required_language.resource_geography: Use potential or reconstructed resource opportunity, not realized butterfly range.
required_language.anthropogenic: Attribute expansion to introduced host distributions in the reconstructed opportunity surface, not causal butterfly expansion.
required_language.climate: Use filtering or association language, not proof of physiological causation.
required_language.negative_primary: State that the pilot-derived host-breadth climate-release hypothesis was not supported, not that host breadth has exactly zero effect.

questions.question: Does anthropogenic redistribution of larval host plants disproportionately expand geographic resource opportunity for butterflies with broader taxonomic host breadth?
questions.outcome: large reconstructed expansion, but proportional expansion nearly unrelated to host-family breadth

questions.question: Why can taxonomic host specialists and generalists gain similar proportional geographic resource opportunity from anthropogenic host redistribution?
questions.timing: generated after Q1 aggregate result and frozen before host-contribution decomposition
questions.outcome: specialists show more concentrated and generalists more distributed host-contribution architecture

questions.question: Within a fixed level of host-family breadth, does host-species richness still predict anthropogenic opportunity architecture?
questions.timing: generated after Q2 mechanism result and frozen before within-stratum associations
questions.outcome: strong within-category portfolio-architecture gradient; structural bounds explicitly acknowledged

questions.question: How closely does family-level diet breadth correspond to geographic larval-resource breadth?
questions.timing: early exploratory inspection of exact resource reconstruction
questions.outcome: partial coupling with substantial rank discordance

questions.question: Is climate-associated filtering common within contemporary host-resource opportunity?
questions.timing: separate independent climate route after panel freeze

questions.question: Does broader host-family breadth weaken climate-associated filtering within host-resource opportunity?
questions.timing: pilot-derived hypothesis frozen before independent-panel response
